profile.research_note:
Operator field corrected from blank to Stack Infrastructure based on the facility own name (source data left operator blank). Reused operator-level research from twoai_dc_operators row: Stack Infrastructure.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] STACK Infrastructure launched on January 16, 2019, when IPI Partners, a joint venture between Iron Point and Iconiq Capital, combined the assets of Infomart Data Centers and T5 Data Centers into a single wholesale colocation platform. The company is commonly reported as headquartered in Denver, Colorado, though this entry did not independently confirm that address against a primary source this session.

STACKs own site describes a global footprint of 22 locations across three regions, 10 in the Americas, 7 in EMEA, and 5 in Asia Pacific, without stating a founding year, headquarters address, or aggregate capacity figure on the fetched page itself.

The registry here tracks 11 STACK facilities across four states, California, Illinois, Oregon, and Virginia, a subset of its ten Americas locations. As with CyrusOne, QTS, and DataBank elsewhere in this registry, STACKs formation by combining two predecessor operators, Infomart and T5, under new private-equity ownership is a pattern worth checking against this registrys facility-level data: any STACK facility with legacy Infomart or T5 branding should be recorded with a former_operator note rather than treated as a STACK-only history. This specific facility, recorded in this registry as STACK New Albany in Franklin County, OH, was not individually named in the operator-level research above; its operator field was blank in the source data and is corrected here to Stack Infrastructure based on the facility own name, which unambiguously identifies its operator brand. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.
